body.heading: How the chain works
paragraphs: Sit in a circle with your family. The first person gives the next person a true compliment — something they really do well or a kind thing they did.
That person says thank you, then gives a compliment to the next person. The kindness travels around the circle like links joining into a chain.

body.heading: Make it visible
paragraphs: If you have string, the compliment-giver can hold one end and pass the ball along. Soon a web of string links everyone together.
Look at your string web. That is what kindness does in a family — it connects everyone to everyone else.

body.heading: Harder rounds
paragraphs: Try a round where every compliment must be about something the person did this week. Or try a silent round with kind actions instead of words.
Notice how the room feels after the game. Compliments are small, but a whole chain of them is strong.

takeaway: A chain of true compliments links a family together, and every link makes the chain stronger.
safetyNotes: This is a talking game — the only rule is that every compliment must be kind and true.
screenFreeExtension: Start a compliment chain at the dinner table tonight with one kind sentence each.
